shill: cellular: respect authentication method in APN property A user-specific APN is provided to shill through setting the APN property of a cellular service object. The APN property is a dictionary that contains the APN name and other optional entries such as username, password, and authentication method. CL:857742 and CL:857743 added the support for APN authentication method specified in the mobile operator database. This CL updates shill to respect the authentication method in the user-specified APN property. Once the corresponding support is added to the Chrome network settings UI, a user will be able to specify the authentication method for a custom APN. BUG=b:68680371 TEST=Run unit tests. TEST=Verify that shill preserves the authentication method specified through the APN property of a cellular service. Nami: Toggle Anx7447 reset line at start-up This patch configures the GPIO pin connected to the reset pin of Anx7447 as push-pull low. When the EC start up from reset, it pulls it high, waits for 1 msec, then pulls it low. This allows the tcpc to recover from a hang and guarantees it to start from a known state. Signed-off-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> BUG=b:79868559 BRANCH=none TEST=Verify Anx7447 port charges on Nami with a rework. CHROMIUM: ath10k: add a knob to toggle PS-POLL station kickout logic in FW Firmware notes down the last received frame from the station before it has gone into power save. If the STA wakes up and sends a PS-POLL frame (indicating it has exited from powersave) after 150secs,STA will be kicked out. This knob will toggle the PS-POLL station kickout logic in FW. This is helpful in debugging/testing issues. You can enable the ps-poll kickout logic for a station as below: echo 0|1 > /sys/kernel/debug/ieee80211/phy0/netdev\:wlan-2400mhz/stations/ {mac_address_of_station}/pspoll_sta_ko_enable Here 1 indicates enabling the PS-POLL station kickout logic and 0 indicates disabling the PS-POLL station kickout logic BUG=chrome-os-partner:62036 TEST= Connect a 2x2 client to the AP. Run traffic. After sometime, make sure the client has gone to power save and wakes up by sending PS-poll only after 150secs. You should see the PS-poll inactivity kickout. Using above debugfs knob toggle the pspoll station kickout in FW and test if the kickout is turned off or on appropriately Change-Id: I1dffb5f0a3b18035d630268cd31620856f5df84a Signed-off-by: Ashok Raj Nagarajan <arnagara@codeaurora.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/809444 Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Tested-by: s.sudharshan s.sudharshan <s.sudharshan@globaledgesoftware.corp-partner.google.com> Reviewed-by: Srinivasa duvvuri <sduvvuri@google.com> Reviewed-by: Dheeraj KM <dheeraj.km@globaledgesoft.com>

cros-disks: Get the realpath of the parent if the datadir doesn't exist. When mounting DriveFS, on the first mount for a particular datadir, cros-disks is responsible for creating that directory. Currently, it attempts to find the realpath of the datadir, which fails before it has been created. When the datadir doesn't exist, find the realpath of the parent directory instead. BUG=chromium:829274 TEST=unit tests Change-Id: I3daf27f69ebd85d18f5a47cbe31033d8255e39e3 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1071151 Commit-Ready: Sam McNally <sammc@chromium.org> Tested-by: Sam McNally <sammc@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ben Chan <benchan@chromium.org>

cryptohome: Create GCache/v2 and make it writable by chronos-access. The new drive integration (DriveFS) runs as a separate user, mounted via cros-disks. cros-disks will be responsible for creating a directory within the user's cryptohome to store the metadata and caches: GCache/v2/<mount ID>. cros-disks is a member of chronos-access, but GCache is not group writable, so it cannot create the v2 directory itself. Change cryptohome to create GCache/v2 with group chronos-access and make it group writable as well as accessible, giving system daemons, including cros-disks, write access to GCache/v2. BUG=chromium:829274 TEST=Log into chrome, verify GCache/v2 exists within the user's cryptohome, has group chronos-access and is group writable Change-Id: I3b63fd2d77d587f4f86219bb0f8d9c096c45af6a Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1051128 Commit-Ready: Sam McNally <sammc@chromium.org> Tested-by: Sam McNally <sammc@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Gwendal Grignou <gwendal@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jorge Lucangeli Obes <jorgelo@chromium.org>

vm_tools: Refactor part of concierge into cicerone This refactors all of the container communication that is done in concierge into cicerone. It is still expected that Chrome will only be calling into concierge, so all cicerone calls get proxied from concierge into cicerone. After this CL lands, then we can update Chrome to using cicerone instead of concierge where relevant. After Chrome OS is then uprev'd to that version of Chrome, we can then remove all the proxying to cicerone from concierge. This CL also needs crrev.com/c/1069772 to land and Chrome OS uprev'd to include it before it is merged so that Chrome receives the cicerone ContainerStarted signal and understands it.
